titulo: The Oct 2026 map: computer use, extensions, browsers with an agent, and dev tools
lead: Browser agent has become several different things: a model that looks at the screen, an extension in your Chrome, a whole browser with an agent inside, and tools that give a browser to Claude Code or Codex. In this lesson you separate the four families, read each one's status with a date, and get the course kit ready.
objetivo: place computer use, extensions, browsers with an agent, and dev tools, with a dated status, and get the kit ready.

aprende.t: The four families of browser agents
Status with a source and a date, no rumors
The kit: Playwright MCP and Chrome DevTools MCP with a pinned version
Why this course tests with the dev tools

hero_alt: Dark monitor with four browser windows side by side, each with a different panel, under neutral light.

nos.detalhe: The model receives screenshots and returns clicks and keystrokes. It works for any program, but it's the most expensive and fragile way. The reference benchmark is OSWorld: in the original paper, humans completed 72.36% of the tasks and the best model of the time, 12.24%. OSWorld 2.0 came out on 06/26/2026; the current scoreboard wasn't checked here.

An agent inside the browser you already use. Claude for Chrome went from preview to beta on the Max plan on 11/24/2025, according to Anthropic, in the same post where it says no browser agent is immune to prompt injection.

The agent lives inside the browser: a browser built around it, like ChatGPT Atlas (OpenAI), or a feature of Chrome itself, like auto browse (Google). Both show up in press coverage; the primary pages were not read, so they stay as reported, not confirmed on 10/19/2026.

MCP servers that give your coding agent a browser: Playwright MCP (Microsoft, reads the accessibility tree) and Chrome DevTools MCP (Google, console, network, and performance). These are the ones the course uses: they run on your machine, with a pinned version, against local pages.

secoes.legenda: All four reach the same HTML. What you test with the fourth holds, in large part, for the other three.
secoes.dica: Status as of Oct 2026 changes fast: everything here has a source and a date.

secoes.titulo: How to read an agent's status
secoes.sub: Three questions before you believe it.

texto: A post from the maker, the documentation, or the official repository counts as fact. A press article or an aggregator counts as "reported by."
Example: Anthropic's 11/24/2025 post is a primary source; OpenAI's post about Atlas (12/22/2025) only reached us here through press coverage.
Write the date next to the status: "beta on the Max plan on 11/24/2025," not "it's in beta." In six months the sentence without a date becomes a lie.
A package version is status too: the kit pins @playwright/mcp 0.0.83 and chrome-devtools-mcp 1.10.1, published on 09/28 and 09/23/2026 according to the npm registry.
An extension or a browser with an agent runs on someone's account and uses up a subscription. The dev tools run locally, against 127.0.0.1, with no model at all if you want.
That is why the course rehearses everything with them and leaves the real agent for an optional step.

exemplo.texto: A browser agent only against the kit's page or against a site of your own. No real logins, purchases, or third-party forms.

secoes.titulo: The ready kit in two commands
secoes.sub: Installs the pinned versions and checks the pieces. The versoes.mjs script calls no network and no model.

blocos.conteudo:
[ -d ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-navegador-v72 ] || git clone -q https://github.com/inematds/formacao-webmcp-navegador-v72 ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-navegador-v72
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-navegador-v72/kit
npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npx playwright install chromium; echo "saída: $?"

Four required pieces: Node 20.19+, 22.12+ or 23+ (chrome-devtools-mcp requires it), Playwright with its own Chromium, Playwright MCP, and Chrome DevTools MCP. Claude Code and Codex show up as optional: the whole course runs without them.

npm ci installs exactly what is in package-lock.json. The first time, npx playwright install chromium downloads Playwright's Chromium (a few hundred MB); after that, it prints nothing.

secoes.sub: The kit on your machine and your map. Each exercise has a "done when".

exercicios.texto: Run both blocks. If a piece is missing, its line starts with "falta:" and says what to do.
exercicios.pronto: node versoes.mjs → kit pronto: 4 de 4 peças obrigatórias and saída: 0.

exercicios.texto: Create mapa-agentes.md with three browser agents that you or your clients use, one line per agent: family | agent | status | source | date. A status without a source becomes "reported by."
exercicios.pronto: grep -c "|" mapa-agentes.md → 3 or more, and every line has a date.

perguntas.p: Which agent family does this course use to test the site, and why?
opcoes: Computer use, because it works with any program on the machine
Dev tools, because they run locally, with a pinned version
Browser with an agent, because it's what the end customer uses
Extensions, because they already come installed in every Chrome
perguntas.explica: Playwright MCP and Chrome DevTools MCP run on your machine, against 127.0.0.1, and you can rehearse them without a model. The other families run on someone's account and use up a subscription.

perguntas.p: You read in an article that a browser with an agent came to Android in August. How do you write that on your map?
opcoes: As fact, if the article is from a well-known, trusted site
You don't write it: press news is never useful
As fact, as long as another article repeats the date
perguntas.explica: Without the primary source, it goes in as reported, with the date you checked. Two articles that copy the same source are still secondhand.

perguntas.p: What did Anthropic say on 11/24/2025 about browser agents and prompt injection?
opcoes: That no browser agent is immune, even with ~1% of attacks succeeding
That the problem was solved in Claude for Chrome
That only extensions are vulnerable; dev tools run isolated and carry no risk
That the risk goes away when the site uses WebMCP
perguntas.explica: The post says the successful attack rate dropped to ~1% and that this "still represents meaningful risk. No browser agent is immune". The topic in depth is covered in course 4.

perguntas.p: Why does the kit pin @playwright/mcp 0.0.83 instead of using the latest version?
opcoes: Because the latest version requires an API key
Because newer versions don't run headless
Because npm blocks installing versions less than a month old
Because the captured output is only valid for the tested version
perguntas.explica: The output of each block was captured with that version, on 10/19/2026. In a newer version, tool names and response format may change.

itens.texto: Computer use, extensions, browsers with an agent, and dev tools all reach the same HTML.
A primary source is fact; the rest is "reported by", with the date you checked.
Playwright MCP and DevTools MCP run on your machine, with a pinned version and without using up your quota.
